problem_type: Duplicate CLI worker options under fair-share admission
symptom: A focused validation run with explicit maxWorkers fails before collection when another Vitest peer exists.
direct_cause: main injects a fair-share maxWorkers option without consuming the existing explicit CLI option; Vitest rejects duplicate singleton options.
class_root: Worker admission budget and caller worker limit are serialized independently instead of producing one authoritative effective option.
affected_population: Parallel focused/default runs with explicit numeric limits
Parallel percentage limits and split/equal argument forms
internal_only_reason: Node child lifecycle and Nomi bounded-owner implementation are directly reproduced with real local fixture children; no inference or external behavior is involved.
invariants: One canonical worker option is emitted under shared admission.
Effective workers never exceed either the caller limit or shared budget.
Exclusive invocation preserves original arguments and Vitest defaults.

door_reduction.why_not: The one CLI owner builds the invocation for all validation entrypoints.

generality_proof: Invocation construction consumes the one singleton option and chooses the smaller resolved worker limit, covering both argument encodings and percentages without caller-specific branches.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Project caller worker preference and fair share into a single invocation.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both invoke the same wrapper; argument forms and percentages are checked against installed Vitest parsing.

recurrence.reason: Every explicit worker limit collides whenever peers>1.
same_class_scan: Inspected pinned Vitest 4.1.8 coverage.DM_a_rWm.js getWorkersCountByPercentage and resolveInlineWorkerOption
Inspected wrapper main and buildVitestInvocation plus all package wrapper callers

prevention.invariant: Only the effective minimum budget is serialized into argv.
prevention.failure_mode: Duplicate or invalid explicit shared-mode worker options fail before launching; no silent over-budget invocation.
prevention.strategy: Move worker option projection into the existing invocation owner and remove main’s blind prepend.

legacy_paths.rationale: Blind option injection is removed; no second runner.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Retain pinned Vitest 4.1.8; percentage conversion matches its installed source. No new dependency is needed.
exit_criteria: Recheck singleton CLI option and percentage worker semantics during the next Vitest upgrade.

migration: No settings or registry format changes.
residual_risks: The existing fair-share minimum-two oversubscription policy is preserved.
